subject: ElevateAI - Capacity phasing options and min-GPU landing plan

From: Jordan Miles <j.miles@elevate.ai>

Cc: procurement@elevate.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — Sizing and ramp for Dedicated cluster (ELEV-8721)

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement here — we need a concise set of committed options and a recommended ramp so we can align finance and infra. High level: ElevateAI expects production traffic to ramp over Q4 and into Q1 (heavy batch embedding jobs overnight + steady low-latency chat traffic daytime).

Questions we need answered for internal approval:
- Minimum GPU footprint you can guarantee for Q4 start (we need a floor for capacity planning).
- Typical onboarding/ramp schedule you recommend if we start Oct 1.
- Pricing deltas for min-floor vs. burst lanes vs. hard reservation.
- Any warmup/run-in credits you provide during the first 30–60 days.

Please attach a one-page comparison so we can drop it into the procurement packet.

Jordan
Procurement Manager, ElevateAI
procurement@elevate.ai

Subject: Re: Initial ask — Sizing and ramp for Dedicated cluster (ELEV-8721)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clarity. I attached a concise options sheet (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf) and captured three pragmatic paths below — each with cluster sizing, minimum GPU floor, typical ramp cadence, and operational notes. Picking one of these should be enough for procurement to estimate CAPEX/OPEX and accept a start date.

Option Alpha — Conservative floor (recommended for predictable cost)- Cluster: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool)- Min GPUs guaranteed: 6 active (soft warm standby for the rest)- Ramp: Week 1: validation & warm-up; Weeks 2–4: scale to 3x baseline traffic; Month 2: full production on 6 GPUs; Month 3: optional 8 GPU steady state- Notes: Best for teams prioritizing SLA and consistent latency. Includes 2 weeks of warmup credits (50% invoice credit) and 30-day onboarding support.

Option Beta — Burst-friendly (cost-balanced)- Cluster: 12 x mixed-precision GPUs (burst lanes + reserved baseline)- Min GPUs guaranteed: 4 active with burst to 12 subject to pre-negotiated burst windows- Ramp: Day 0–14: validation; Day 15–45: measured burst schedule; Month 2: incremental commit to 6 GPUs if stable- Notes: Lower committed floor, good when batch jobs dominate nights; burst windows will be SLAbound.

Option Gamma — Aggressive scale (fast-growth hedge)- Cluster: 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs- Min GPUs guaranteed: 12 active- Ramp: Canary day 0–7; Week 2–6: linear scale to min floor; Month 3+: scale to full cluster or tiered expansion- Notes: For customers with immediate high throughput needs or who will run large embedding refreshes; includes prioritized activation & dedicated escalation channel.

Pricing highlights (see attached):
- Floor pricing is per-GPU-hour applied to the min-guarantee.
- Burst usage billed at on-demand above the cap with pre-agreed overage rates.
- We can structure a blended rate for Alpha if you commit to a 12 month term.

Ask: can you confirm which risk profile Elevate prefers (Conservative / Burst-friendly / Aggressive) and your target contract start date? If you want, Karthik can run a quick burn estimate once you share expected p95 tokens / embedding throughput.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial ask — Sizing and ramp for Dedicated cluster (ELEV-8721)

Monica / Karthik —

Thanks, this helps a lot. Procurement reviewed and prepared redlines — attached (elevate_procurement_redlines.docx). High level feedback: Elevate prefers the Burst-friendly path but needs a clearer definition of burst windows and an explicit warmup/run-in credit structure (procurement wants a holdback equivalent to 10% of first month invoice until we validate baseline). Also asking for a 60-day ramp tolerance in case their embedding refresh schedule slips.

We can be flexible on a 12 month blended commitment if the floor transitions to a smaller guaranteed baseline after month 6. Can you provide a short note on how we handle model/quantization changes mid-contract (risk to performance & billing)?

Jordan

Attachments: elevate_procurement_redlines.docx
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <j.miles@elevate.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — Sizing and ramp for Dedicated cluster (ELEV-8721)

Jordan —

Appreciate the redlines. Quick responses inline and next steps below: 

- Burst windows: we will define two guaranteed burst windows per 24h (00:00–06:00 and 22:00–23:59 PST) with contractual latency SLOs for those windows. Additional bursts outside these windows are allowed as on-demand at pre-agreed overage rates.

- Warmup/run-in credits: we can accommodate a 10% holdback reversed after 30 days of validated baseline performance; alternatively, we can offer a 5% immediate onboarding credit plus 5% holdback.

- 60-day ramp tolerance: accepted. We will codify a 60-day flexible ramp period with monthly checkpoints; if usage does not meet checkpoints, the transition to a smaller baseline may be negotiated.

- Model/quantization changes: any model architecture change that materially affects GPU utilization or latency will trigger a joint change-control item. We will run a three-point evaluation (perf delta, cost delta, rollback plan). If a customer-requested model change increases resource needs, overage billing applies from the change date unless a formal rework is agreed. Rishi (engineering) will add a short runbook to the SOW for this.

Next steps: Karthik will produce a burn estimate for the Burst-friendly path and an updated option sheet with the two warmup credit variants by EOD Tue. If that looks good, we can send a term sheet to legal and target an Oct 15 activation window.

I'll loop in legal once Karthik posts the numbers. Thanks — good momentum.

Monica Patel
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf, elevate_procurement_redlines.docx
